Name: Adult Skull Dragon
Source: Lyres Guide to Risk and Reward
Information:
**Skull Dragons**

Skull dragons, perhaps named a bit obviously for their appearance, were originally the result of an insane necromancer’s research. This unhinged researcher, an elven archmage named Satorium, chronicled that he had dreams where a ghastly undead dragon spoke to him, commanding him to create a body for it to inhabit. The beast promised him rule of the Somonian empire - a promise that appealed to the vainglorious elf. He stole dragon eggs and experimented on them, trying to remove their souls before birth to create a suitable body for his master. He failed, however, and instead the dragons born from this process were twisted into dragons that live and breathe undeath. Satorium was killed by his own creations, which went on to pass their newly corrupted genetics to all wyrmlings they would sire.

Skull dragons have dark, oily scales covered in segments of steel-hard chitin that resembles bone, giving them a powerful defensive exoskeleton. Their heads feature twisting horns of many descriptions. They are gluttonous beasts that are endowed with an endless hunger, which their long life becomes centered upon.

**Corpse Eater.** Skull dragons prefer not to eat meat fresh, if they can help it; they take delight in consuming the flesh and bones of creatures that have been allowed to decay for some time. Their lairs invariably always have chambers devoted to aging meat, where they hang corpses from the walls and ceiling like a butcher.

As a skull dragon ages, it develops an appetite for corpses that have accumulated greater age. They typically are only truly satisfied when consuming the flesh of something that is roughly as old as they are. This quirk leads them to aim to feed specifically on long-living species such as elves and nephilim, and also makes them the natural enemy of other dragons. All dragons - gem, chromatic, and metallic - understand that a skull dragon’s hunger makes them an eventual enemy: an apex predator among apex predators. So great is their hunger that, like a black widow, they are a threat even to their own mates and wyrmlings if starved. Should they ever reach the status of a greatwyrm, they would set their eyes upon the very gods.

**Undead Defilers.** The skull dragon can manipulate the forces of death to suit its needs: its breath weapon seeps into every pore of those it kills, raising them as undead beasts under the dragon’s control. Furthermore, when an undead beast dies around it, the dragon can absorb the necromantic energy that holds their being together to satiate its own hunger. For this purpose, skull dragons enjoy consuming undead when possible. They will often keep those they kill as undead pets to be consumed at a later date.

**A Skull Dragon’s Lair**

Skull dragons make their lairs in a way that might remind other creatures of graves. They burrow into the earth, creating large chambers where they often prop up the skeletal remains of their conquests, and adorn them with the wealth they gather. Particularly nefarious skull dragons dig their lairs under large graveyards or mausoleums so they have open access to the dead. They enjoy being in the presence of corpses - particularly ancient ones.

**Regional Effects**

The region containing a legendary skull dragon’s lair is warped by the dragon’s magic, which creates one or more of the following effects:

• A humanoid creature that is killed within 10 miles of the dragon’s lair rises up again in 24 hours as an undead beast, and the dragon becomes aware of it.
• Creatures who rest for 8 hours or longer within 6 miles of the dragon’s lair feel an aching in their bones until next time they rest, causing them to feel stiff and brittle.
• Necromantic spells and any effect that deals necrotic damage within 1 mile of the dragon’s lair become more dramatic. Necrotic energy glows with a reddish hue, and all necromantic spells take on a new, terrifying life as if the magic has a will of its own.

If the dragon dies, these effects end immediately.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes three attacks: one with its Bite and two with its Claws.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 6 (1d10) necrotic damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Frightful Presence
actions.description: Each creature of the dragon’s choice that is within 120 feet of the dragon and aware of it must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature’s saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon’s Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Decay Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: The dragon exhales necrotic gas in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that cone must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw, taking 66 (12d10) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that is killed by this damage raises on initiative count 20 as a zombie or suitable undead creature under the dragon’s control, and rolls a new initiative.

actions.name: Swallow
actions.description:
The dragon swallows one Medium or smaller creature it is grappling. It can hold up to three Medium creatures in its body. In place of each Medium creature it can hold two Small creatures or four Tiny creatures.

A creature the dragon has swallowed is restrained and blinded while inside it, and has total cover. They take 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of their turns. If the dragon takes 30 damage or more in a single turn from a swallowed creature, it must succeed a DC 15 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature into a space adjacent to it, where they fall prone. If it dies, the effect ends and creatures can escape its body by spending 15 feet of movement.

reactions.name: Consume Undeath
reactions.description: If an undead creature dies within 30 feet of the dragon, it can absorb necrotic energy from it, causing the dragon to regain 1d8 hit points multiplied by the creature’s CR rating and/or class level.

options.name: Detect
options.description: The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

options.name: Attack
options.description: The dragon makes a Claw attack.

options.name: Predation (Costs 2 Actions)
options.description: The dragon attempts a grapple check against one creature within range. If it wins, the target is restrained and grappled by the dragon until the end of the dragon’s next turn.

entries.name: Legendary Reaction
entries.description: When the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

legendary_reactions.source_conversion_note: Converted from Legendary Reactions (3/Day) per standing formatting rule.

lair_actions.intro: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row.

options.name: Desperate Exhumation
options.description: Up to four creatures the dragon can see are assailed by corpses that pull themselves from the walls and floor, grasping at them. Each target must succeed a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be restrained until the next time the dragon takes a lair action. Creatures trapped this way can use their action to attempt a DC 15 Strength check, breaking free on a success.

options.name: Grave Hunt
options.description: The dragon identifies the scents and sounds of everything within its lair, causing it to become aware of every creature’s location within 120 feet as if it has succeeded a Wisdom (Perception) check against them. Until initiative count 20 the following round, creatures cannot benefit from hiding from the dragon, and it can see invisible creatures as if they were plainly visible.

options.name: Rot Pile
options.description: A mound of rotting vegetation and flesh erupts from the walls of the lair, centered on a particular point, spreading a sickening ichor in a 20-foot-radius. Each creature within range must succeed a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 4 (1d6) poison damage multiplied by the dragon’s proficiency bonus on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
